description: We’re a team of 5 taking on “Abandoned but Not Forgotten”: a senior software engineer, a storyteller, a 3D designer, a UI/UX designer, and an AI/backend dev. We’re building an interactive 3D journey where NASA’s retired hardware, from Voyager to Mars rovers, tells its own story to kids. Join us if you love space and storytelling. We’re looking for Three.js/Blender skills, science communication or education experience, and video/sound editing.
summary:
ATHAR is an interactive memorial garden for five real NASA explorers represented through four mission stories: Eagle, Pioneer 10, Spirit and Opportunity together, and Ingenuity. Visitors can explore a 3D garden, follow a guided story, examine mission timelines and scientific facts, and listen to optional first-person narration.

The project addresses the challenge of making space exploration accessible and memorable by turning mission data into an engaging experience for learners of different ages. It connects each explorer’s discoveries, challenges, and legacy to the real science behind the missions, while clearly distinguishing verified facts from creative storytelling.

ATHAR matters because these missions continue to teach us long after their hardware has stopped working. By preserving their stories in an interactive, bilingual experience, the project helps more people discover how exploration advances science—and how every mission leaves knowledge for the next.
details:
ATHAR is an interactive, bilingual memorial garden for NASA’s robotic explorers. Visitors can explore a 3D garden, open mission stories, and learn about Eagle, Pioneer 10, Spirit and Opportunity together, and Ingenuity. Each story combines mission timelines, scientific facts, and optional first-person narration, helping make space exploration approachable for children and adults.

The project’s benefit is that it turns mission information into an experience people can explore at their own pace. Its intended impact is to preserve the explorers’ legacies, encourage curiosity about planetary science, and show how discoveries from one mission can inform future exploration.

We built ATHAR with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using browser-based 3D graphics and custom-drawn rover and spacecraft models. The creative approach blends a welcoming garden setting, character-led storytelling, interactive visuals, and clear distinctions between verified facts and imaginative narration. We considered accessibility, Arabic and English support, mobile layouts, user control over sound, and presenting scientific information in a way that is engaging without losing its grounding in real missions.
